userPriority: delivery-app and retail-market prices first; government sources are secondary helpers

summary.practicalFastPath: Start with willing local retailers that can provide a POS/export CSV or merchant-authorized read access to their Salla/Zid catalog. Capture each merchant/store identity and observation time. Use delivery-platform partner APIs only for that merchant's own contracted vendor catalog. These documented APIs are not a verified public read-any-store/city catalog feed.
summary.consumerCatalogBoundary: A consumer-facing catalog can be browsed in the platform app for a selected service area, but the official HungerStation terms prohibit copying merchant-listing content for republication and warn the displayed menu can differ from what is actually offered. No public consumer bulk-read API was confirmed in this bounded review; that is not proof that none exists.
summary.freshnessRule: Persist source, store/branch, checkedAt, currency, product/pack identity, price kind (regular/sale), and availability. Re-fetch on a short interval agreed with each feed owner; show the last-checked time. An API's real-time update capability is not a guarantee of consumer checkout price or a source freshness SLA.
smallShopRecommendation: For an independent shop, request a permitted CSV/POS export first. Keep a store-specific read-only feed and price/stock timestamps.
If the merchant runs Salla or Zid, offer a merchant-authorized OAuth/app connection with the narrow products.read scope for that merchant's own catalog.

If the shop wants orders through an aggregator, apply through the merchant onboarding route first; use its vendor portal or approved API/SFTP integration for its own outlet data. Confirm commission, contract scope, and supported cities directly with the platform before relying on it.
Do not treat an aggregator consumer app as permission to bulk copy/re-publish other merchants' catalogs or prices.

geography.coverageEvidence: Partner application says availability is checked during merchant registration for the merchant's area; exact supported-city list was not present in the reviewed page.
geography.branchScope: Partner catalog endpoints are keyed by chain_id and vendor_id; data is scoped to the merchant chain/outlet, not every consumer-visible store in a city.

publicConsumerCatalog.consumerCanBrowse: Platform terms describe stores in the user's local area and menus available for ordering.
publicConsumerCatalog.reuseBoundary: Terms prohibit copying store-listing content for republication. They also state the displayed menu may not match what the merchant actually provides.
publicConsumerCatalog.interpretation: No official consumer catalog API for reading all stores/cities/prices was confirmed in this review; absence is not proven. Do not scrape or use hidden endpoints.

documentedOptions: self-service vendor tools for smaller shops
merchantIntegration.read: Catalog use-case docs list GET to retrieve the partner's available products and export an assortment snapshot.
merchantIntegration.write: Partner API supports PUT single/bulk product catalog updates; fields include SKU, barcode, quantity reference, price, active state, and maximum sales quantity. Updates are asynchronous; bulk completion can be reported by webhook.
merchantIntegration.pricingAndAvailability: Partner API overview describes real-time availability/stock and product price synchronization. The docs say the quantity field in the catalog update acts as a reference against a configured sales buffer and is not stored as stock quantity.
merchantIntegration.otherPartnerFunctions: Orders can be received and tracked in real time; outlet open/closed status, schedules, closures, and busy mode can be managed through partner integrations.
merchantIntegration.authAndRequirements: Must already be a partner and have Partner Portal plus Integrations Plugin access. Documentation describes chain/vendor IDs and OAuth2 credentials issued/generated via Partner Portal or account manager. Partner signup asks for a valid commercial registration, Saudi national ID, product photos, logo, menu, and branch coordinates; tax certificate, authorization, and IBAN are listed when applicable.
merchantIntegration.smallMerchantRoute: HungerStation's Local Shops docs say smaller partners commonly use self-service tools; API/SFTP is for automating catalog/order/promotion work. SFTP is structured CSV and needs no API development, but still is a partner-side integration to that merchant's own assortment.
merchantIntegration.freshnessAndLimits: Real-time is the documented partner synchronization capability, not a published freshness SLA for consumer prices. Catalog update endpoints return queued job IDs; observe completion before assuming an update is live. Exact per-outlet coverage depends on the merchant vendor IDs and approved partner access.
merchantIntegration.fees: Partner onboarding describes commission but gives no percentage in the reviewed page. Consumer terms say displayed item prices are current at order time and may later change; delivery/small-order/service/payment fees can be added, shown before checkout, and service fee can vary by customer distance. Treat product price separately from delivery/platform fees.

geography.countryFocus: Saudi merchant platform; source documents the Salla merchant API generally, not a citywide retail feed
geography.coverageEvidence: A merchant-authorized Salla store at a time; API page says products related to your store.
geography.branchScope: The list-products endpoint is store-scoped; no branch-specific price coverage was confirmed in the reviewed endpoint. Store delivery zones/branch variation require separate merchant agreement or additional APIs.

catalogRead.filteringAndPagination: Keyword, status, category, page, and per_page parameters are documented; response includes pagination.
catalogRead.authAndRequirements: Salla says Merchant APIs require a verified Salla Partners account and OAuth2.0. The merchant must install/authorize the app and grant the requested store scope; access can be revoked by the merchant. Published app authorization uses Salla's Easy Mode.
catalogRead.freshnessAndLimits: The API returns the store's current catalog response when read; documentation reviewed did not state an update freshness SLA or push notification for price changes. Poll/webhook only with merchant authorization and platform rules; save checkedAt and don't call it live checkout price.
catalogRead.fees: API docs reviewed do not specify Salla merchant subscription, app, or integration fees; confirm separately.

sources.title: Salla Merchant API Security Considerations

geography.countryFocus: Saudi merchant platform; reviewed API is store-scoped, not a citywide listing feed
geography.coverageEvidence: GET /v1/products/ request requires a Store-Id and access token.
geography.branchScope: The product-list endpoint is scoped to a store; branch-specific catalog/price coverage was not established in the reviewed page.

catalogRead.authAndRequirements: The official endpoint documentation shows Access-Token, Store-Id, and Manager role headers and requires products.read. Merchant authorization/credential issuance details should be confirmed with the merchant/Zid; no credential was requested or used for this review.
catalogRead.freshnessAndLimits: List response is paginated and can be filtered by stock and price. The docs reviewed do not state price freshness SLA or change timestamps; record checkedAt and confirm whether webhooks are available to the authorized merchant integration.
catalogRead.fees: API documentation reviewed does not state Zid subscription/app/integration fees; confirm separately.

integrations.sourceClass: provider mini-app partnership, not a public grocery-catalog reader

geography.coverageEvidence: Application asks providers which cities they serve and operational capacity; sources do not publish a definitive supported-city list.

programFacts.whatItIs: A service-provider mini-app integrated inside Nana, with APIs/templates for catalog, service areas, pricing, and order status.
programFacts.catalogReadAnyStore: Not documented in reviewed sources; this is a route for a provider's own storefront/service, not a cross-store grocery price feed.
programFacts.requirements: Apply, describe service/cities/capacity, build using APIs/templates or own developer, pass business verification and quality/safety review, and receive a controlled rollout. Developer docs say Nana supplies SDK access/credentials and conducts code review.
programFacts.feesAndFreshness: No fee schedule or catalog freshness SLA found in the reviewed sources; terms need confirmation with Nana before relying on this route.

dataCaptureContract.missingFieldBehavior: Keep unknown fields null; never infer product pack size, branch coverage, delivery fees, tax inclusion, or live status.
dataCaptureContract.pricePresentation: Display last-checked timestamp and separate item price from delivery, service, small-order, and payment fees.

unresolved: No official public API for bulk-reading all consumer stores and prices across a Saudi city was confirmed. This bounded search does not prove none exists.
Exact HungerStation commission rate, supported city list, partner access contract, and any third-party reuse rights require merchant/platform agreement.
Salla and Zid endpoint examples provide merchant-store data; branch-level availability/pricing and API fee terms were not established from the cited pages.
Nana's city coverage, commercial terms, and any app-specific feed freshness terms remain unverified.
A consumer-visible delivery price may change with store selection, stock, promotion, delivery area, distance, or checkout fees; app terms do not guarantee the displayed menu matches fulfillment.
